text:
sofia: Quick idea — create a partner-contrib scaffold repo for cloud marketplace / HW partners to submit reference templates + a lightweight test matrix. Keeps our curated refkits consistent and speeds partner onboarding.

sofia: Goals: standardized module layout, CI checks (fmt/lint/plan), minimal example overlay per cloud/hw, and a CONTRIBUTING + CLA flow.

tariq: +1. Curious about scope — just terraform modules or also sample apps and docs?

sofia: Start with Terraform modules + README-driven examples. If partners want app samples, we can add an "examples/" folder later. Focus on guardrails first.

alex: Sounds good. For CI we should enforce: terraform fmt, tflint, static plan check (no creds), and a lightweight plan against a mocked backend. Also multi-arch validation (x86/arm) for any container builds.

jen: I can draft the CONTRIBUTING + CLA template. Also propose a minimal GitHub Actions file so partners get immediate feedback. Example action: 

```yaml
name: iaac-validate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: Terraform fmt
        run: terraform fmt -check -recursive
      - name: TFLint
        run: tflint --config .tflint.hcl
      - name: Static plan (no creds)
        run: terraform init -backend=false && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan || true
```

sofia: Nice. For partner overlays, we want one per cloud (aws/gcp/azure) + hw tag (ampere/graviton). Each overlay is just a minimal vars file + doc.

alex: We'll provide a small module scaffold: module manifest, example usage, and inputs/outputs docs. Example usage snippet: 

```hcl
module "refkit_example" {
  source  = "git::https://github.com/redwood/partner-scaffold//modules/refkit?ref=v0.1.0"
  region  = var.region
  flavor  = "gpu-small"
}
```

tariq: Policy questions: do partners commit to Redwood-approved license? Is CLA mandatory? We need legal sign-off before opening.

jen: I'll coordinate with legal. My preference: MIT + CLA for first-party contributions, then switch to DCO if partners prefer.

sofia: Ops ask — add a required badge matrix in README showing which overlays have been smoke-tested and their test status. We can automate badge updates via a small release workflow.

alex: I'll prototype a smoke test that runs a plan (no apply) and a docker build for example containers on both amd64/arm64 runners. Will post PR later today.

ci-bot: GitHub action run queued for branch "scaffold/prototype" — check logs at https://github.com/redwood/partner-scaffold/actions

tariq: Next steps: jen/legal on CLA, alex prototype CI + smoke tests, sofia to write partner README + onboarding checklist. Sync back end of week? :calendar: 

sofia: Yep — EOW sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
